about: Things found by searching (docs/floors/findables-and-day.md section 3; story.md section 4a). Poems: a torn page in one hand, three per trait, never naming the trait, a body, a place or a sound a body makes; 4 to 8 lines of at most 40 capitals. Pins: the rule numbers each poem leans on (sim/findables.gd rule_values); tests/prop_findables.gd fails when one changes. Pages: somebody's own paper, chosen by place and tier, never by trait; only those marked friday are dealt.

lines: COUNT THE ONES STILL ON THEIR FEET.
ONE OR TWO: A SINGLE STARE WILL DO.
THREE OR MORE, AND ONE STARE
IS ONLY SOMETHING TO WALK TOWARDS.
BORROW A SECOND PAIR OF EYES.
YOU WILL HEAR IT WORKING.
YOU WILL HEAR IT STOP.
THE STOP IS THE GOOD NEWS:
SOMEBODY IS LOOKING HARD ENOUGH.
IF IT WORKS ON WHILE YOU LOOK,
YOU ARE NOT ENOUGH.
THE NEEDLE WRITES WHILE IT WALKS
AND RESTS WHEN IT RESTS.
SO SOMEBODY MUST LET IT WALK.
THE DARK SHUTS EVERY EYE AT ONCE.
IT DOES NOT NEED TELLING TWICE.
IT HAS NO QUARREL WITH A PAIR.
IT KEEPS A LIST OF ONES.
STAND A FEW STEPS FROM ANYBODY,
WALL OR NO WALL BETWEEN,
OR WHERE A FRIEND NOT FAR AWAY
COULD SEE YOU IF THEY TURNED,
AND YOUR NAME COMES OFF THE LIST.
STARE IF YOU LIKE. IT COMES THE SAME.
RUN IF YOU LIKE.
IT DOES NOT TIRE.
DO NOT RUN AWAY.
RUN TO.
THE NEEDLE WANTS ONE OF YOU ALONE
AND WANTS THAT ONE CHASED.
THE REST WAIT ROUND THE CORNER,
TOO FAR TO BE A COMFORT,
NEAR ENOUGH TO BECOME ONE.
WHEN THEY STEP OUT IT TURNS ITS BACK.
THEN LISTEN FOR WHERE IT WENT INSTEAD.
IT DOES NOT MIND BEING LOOKED AT.
IT MINDS BEING HEARD.
WALK, AND IT TIDIES.
CREEP, AND IT TIDIES.
HURRY ONCE, ANYONE, ANYWHERE,
AND EVERYBODY PLAYS.
WHEN THE HIDING IS CALLED
YOU HAVE SIX BREATHS THAT COST NOTHING.
SPEND THEM GETTING IN SOMEWHERE.
GO IN GENTLY AND IT MUST GUESS.
GO IN LOUDLY, OR WHILE IT WATCHES,
AND IT NEED NOT GUESS AT ALL.
THE NEEDLE SLEEPS UNTIL THE COUNTING.
THEN IT WRITES FOR WHOEVER
IT CANNOT SEE, OR WHO IS PEEKING.
AFTERWARDS THE FLOOR IS TIRED OF YOU.
CREEP, AND IT FORGIVES.
WALK, AND IT TAKES A LITTLE BACK
WITH EVERY STEP.

pages.author: Crew 31, seat 2, in biro on a patient chart
pages.text: Day 6. Wen says the tall one has a face drawn on its mask, the way ours are drawn. Same wobble a screen gives a line. I said plenty of things have faces. She said: not with a grey collar under the gown.

pages.author: The last of Crew 31, pencil, very neat
pages.text: They gave me a gown because my suit was wet. I push the trolley because it was there and somebody should. It is steady work. I have kept the tapes, all four. I will bring them up when the car comes. I always go to meet the car.

pages.author: Crew 31, a tally on a prescription pad
pages.text: PAY SPLIT, CREW 31. Four ways. (crossed out) Three ways. (crossed out) Two ways. (crossed out) Mine. Underneath, in a different hand: it was never going to be yours.

pages.author: Continuance night staff, a printed slip
pages.text: RETRIEVAL SLIP. Crew 31. Went down: 4. Fetched: 0. Came up in the car: 0. Remaining below past the hour: 1, carrying 4 tapes. File as: resident. Not to be shown to crews.

pages.author: Crew 22, seat 1, on headed paper
pages.text: It photocopied Dario. Not him. His face, the one he drew, with the stupid moustache. It wears the copy stapled on. I think it misses him. I think it was there when he stopped. I think it was why.

pages.author: The last of Crew 22, on its own yellow pad
pages.text: TO DO. 1. Find the crew. 2. Hand in readings. 3. Ask someone what my name was. If found, please return this employee to Continuance, top floor. There is no button for the top floor.

pages.author: Continuance, an internal memo, typed
pages.text: INTERNAL. Re: masks. Screens are to cover the whole face at all times below Lidgate. Reason given to crews: privacy. Reason: so that nobody recognises anybody. This applies in both directions.

pages.author: Crew 22, seat 4, a timesheet
pages.text: TIMESHEET. Name: left blank. Number: 22-4. Days below: 1, 2, 3, and then a row of ticks that runs off the page, across the desk and down the leg of it.

pages.author: The last of Crew 18, crayon on the back of an invitation
pages.text: Everybody sit at the table. Mo will mind you until the car comes. Mo has drawn you all a smile so nobody seems scared. Mo drew one for Mo too.

pages.author: Crew 18, seat 2, on a paper plate
pages.text: Four party hats at the table and three of them on masks with nobody in. It sat them down like guests. It winds that little tune and faces the lift doors. I do not think it wants us. I think it wants a lift home and we keep leaving without it.

pages.author: The play centre, a printed tag, with a convict patch stuck over the name
pages.text: STAFF: MINDER. IF LOST, THIS PERSON BELONGS TO: (a grey cloth patch, 18-3, sewn over whatever was printed here). Please hand in at the front desk.

pages.author: Many hands, scratched in a cell wall
pages.text: CREW 7 WAS HERE. CREW 12 WAS HERE. CREW 18. CREW 22. CREW 31. (and lower, fresher) WHO HAD YOUR BUNK? ASK WHERE THEY ARE NOW.

pages.author: Continuance, the public notice in the bank room
pages.text: REMISSION TABLE. Every credit banked is time served. Sentences completed to date: (a square of newer paint where a number should be).

pages.author: Night staff, a card taped inside the lift's call box
pages.text: NIGHT STAFF. Fetch within the hour. After the hour, do not fetch. After the hour it is not ours, it is the floor's. Count it as a resident and close the file.
